title: Accept products that meet trusted international standards
action: Treat products that meet the standards of other leading economies as complying with Australian mandatory standards, keeping a transparent review where a significant safety risk is identified, and review Australian Standards against the public interest.
why: Australia-only standards make importers and manufacturers redesign, retest and relabel products for a small market, raising prices and limiting choice without a matching safety gain.

evidence.source: 5-year Productivity Inquiry: Advancing Prosperity, Recommendations and Reform Directives
evidence.quote: increasingly accepting product standards adopted in other leading economies as 'deemed to comply', provided that a transparent review could be undertaken in cases where the Australian Government identified a significant safety risk.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: Australian Standards that are not mandated by government should be subject to periodic review against the public interest test (see Recommendation 8) by Standards Australia.
